newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU vets likely to extend Dutch pig ban.
newsitem.headline: EU vets likely to extend Dutch pig ban.

text.p: European Union veterinary experts are expected to extend the EU export ban on Dutch pigs because of swine fever for a week, a Dutch diplomat told Reuters on Wednesday.
The EU standing veterinary committee resumed discussions on the epidemic, which could result in the slaughter of 800,000 pigs, on Wednesday afternoon.
"The veterinary committee is almost certain to extend the ban on Dutch pig exports for another week. That is what we are expecting," the diplomat said.
Last week the EU slapped a ban on the export of live pigs from the Netherlands, except the four northernmost provinces.
The European Commission announced on Tuesday that it would pay 70 per cent towards the cost of slaughtering pigs in the Netherlands and in Germany where an export ban has been set for 60 days.
The vets meeting heard that an inspection team which visited the Netherlands last week had reported that the country's swine fever controls were "excellent".
"That was the word the report used, although there was criticism that insufficient blood samples had been taken at the start of the epidemic," the diplomat added.
